issues.failure_explanation: The stated approximation of the problem with boundary value g instead imposes zero boundary values, and its asserted basis contains only interior-node functions. Since |g|=1, g cannot equal zero. Thus the scheme does not approximate the boundary-value problem introduced immediately before it and cannot directly implement the later nonzero and time-dependent Dirichlet experiments.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a boundary lifting or an affine finite-element space with prescribed boundary nodal values, and consistently modify the scheme, interpolation, test space, and analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The method as defined does not cover the paper's advertised nonhomogeneous Dirichlet problems; a homogeneous-boundary analysis also cannot simply be applied to the unit-length boundary data.
issues.title: The semidiscrete scheme replaces the prescribed unit Dirichlet data by zero data
issues.why_classification: Handling nonhomogeneous data is standard but requires a coherent modification throughout the formulation and error equations rather than a single typographical correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The H3 calculation depends on higher coefficient norms such as ||∇ΔΦ||_2 and ||ΔΦ||_4, not only on ||∇Φ||_∞. Membership in L2_t H3 does not furnish the pointwise-in-time uniform coefficient bounds asserted in the conclusion, and the proof does not retain and integrate their time dependence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the constant with appropriate time-integrable higher norms of Φ and provide an energy/Gronwall argument that keeps those coefficients, or strengthen the hypotheses to uniform H3-type bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniform H3 stability of the auxiliary problem is unsupported and cannot supply uniform regularity for the subsequent fixed-point construction.
issues.title: The auxiliary H3 estimate uses coefficient regularity and uniform bounds not supplied by the lemma
issues.why_classification: A plausible repair exists but requires a nontrivial revised high-order parabolic estimate and materially stronger or more carefully integrated coefficient control.

issues.failure_explanation: For each derivative component, (Φ×∂u)·∂v changes sign when u and v are interchanged. Hence the continuous b-form is skew-symmetric, so b(Φ;u,v)-b(Φ;v,u)=2b(Φ;u,v), generally an O(1) quantity. A consistent discrete form cannot satisfy the asserted O(h) symmetry defect for arbitrary u_h and v_h.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Discard the near-symmetry claim and replace the H1 argument, for example by a valid estimate that exploits skew-symmetry or by deriving H1 control from the L2 estimate and an inverse inequality after the L2 proof is repaired.
issues.overall_effect: The H1 estimate in Proposition pro2, which converts A_h(Φ;ξ,I_h^*∂tξ) into a time derivative using this lemma, is invalid; the main H1 estimate consequently lacks its stated proof.
issues.title: The convection form is skew rather than O(h)-close to symmetric
issues.why_classification: The lemma itself must be substantially weakened or removed, but a contained alternative route to the advertised H1 rate may exist without changing the global method.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimates for J1 and J2 contain one factor of h and only an H1 norm of the solution. They do not imply the h2 estimate required when i=j=1, nor does the proof supply a cancellation or approximation argument producing the extra factor. The final all-(i,j) conclusion therefore exceeds what was established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a new second-order FVEM consistency or duality argument under explicit geometric assumptions is needed, or the L2 rate must be weakened.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h2) L2 error argument in Proposition pro2 uses precisely the unsupported i=j=1 consistency estimate, so the optimal L2 rate and the main theorem are unreliable.
issues.title: The consistency proof establishes only an O(h) bound, not the claimed O(h2) cases
issues.why_classification: The unsupported extra order is central to the advertised optimal L2 estimate, and the source contains neither the needed cancellation argument nor a comparable alternative proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The auxiliary PDE and finite-volume form have diffusion coefficient α, while the continuous form defining R_h has coefficient one and leaves the cross term unscaled. Thus R_h is not the Ritz projection for the operator compared with A_h, and the projection orthogonality used in the error equation does not cancel the relevant continuous operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the continuous bilinear form and Ritz projection with the correct α coefficient, then rederive the projection and consistency estimates for that form.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency identity at the start of Proposition pro2 is not valid for the stated semidiscrete problem, undermining both stated spatial rates.
issues.title: The Ritz form is inconsistent with the alpha-weighted diffusion operator
issues.why_classification: The coefficient correction is conceptually local, but all projection and consistency arguments using the form must be checked and re-established.

issues.failure_explanation: Both the continuous and discrete auxiliary equations contain |∇Φ|², but the consistency decomposition repeatedly uses |Φ|². Consequently the displayed error identity is not obtained by subtracting the two stated equations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every occurrence of |Φ|² in this residual calculation by |∇Φ|² and recheck that the required H1 bounds of the resulting product follow from the stated regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The energy estimates in Proposition pro2 are derived from the wrong residual and do not prove the stated bounds for the auxiliary problem.
issues.title: The auxiliary error equation substitutes |Phi| squared for |grad Phi| squared
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced and local, and the stated regularity is plausibly sufficient for the corrected product estimates, but the inference as written is invalid.

issues.failure_explanation: Testing the error equation with ξ gives (∂tξ,I_h^*ξ), not (∂tξ,ξ). The paper neither proves the FV mass pairing symmetric nor identifies it with the L2 norm. Moreover, its purported norm is defined without a square root: it scales quadratically in ξ but is compared to the linearly scaling L2 norm, which is impossible for arbitrary scalar multiples.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the square-root FV mass norm, prove the needed positivity and symmetry or use its symmetric part, and redo the energy estimate in that norm before invoking norm equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: The basic time-energy identity used for the L2 error estimate is unsupported, so Proposition pro2 and the inherited main estimates do not follow.
issues.title: The proof treats the FV mass pairing as the standard L2 inner product
issues.why_classification: A standard mass-norm argument may repair the step, but the source omits nontrivial structural properties essential to the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem-con only shows that successive iterates of a fixed-point iteration for one backward-Euler equation approach each other. It neither identifies their limit with the continuous-time solution m nor proves convergence of a discrete auxiliary iteration to the nonlinear semidiscrete solution m_h. For fixed τ, the limit solves a backward-Euler algebraic problem, not the continuous PDE at all times.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, provide a direct nonlinear semidiscrete stability/error analysis or a genuine fixed-point construction in a time-dependent function space, with uniform estimates and identification of both continuous and discrete limits.
issues.overall_effect: The transfer of the auxiliary FVEM estimate to the nonlinear LL scheme is unproved, so both main spatial error estimates lack a valid nonlinear convergence argument.
issues.title: The fixed-point argument converges to a backward-Euler step, not to the continuous or semidiscrete LL solutions
issues.why_classification: The missing step is the central bridge from the linear auxiliary analysis to the nonlinear theorem and requires new proof architecture rather than a local correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Even accepting the preceding calculation, a weighted sum of elementwise time derivatives cannot be bounded below by an unweighted sum merely because the positive areas are comparable: individual derivative contributions may have either sign. Applying the asserted inequality to ∂tm_h and to -∂tm_h would force proportionality of the two bilinear forms, which is not established and is generally false. The calculation also loses the factor 1/2 in differentiating a squared gradient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the exchange energy as the exact quadratic form associated with the symmetric part of the discrete stiffness operator and prove an exact derivative identity, or impose mesh conditions under which the form equals a known discrete energy.
issues.overall_effect: The exchange-energy derivative used in the discrete energy proof is not controlled by c_h as claimed, invalidating the principal step in Proposition energy-dissipation.
issues.title: The claimed derivative lower bound for the discrete stiffness form is invalid
issues.why_classification: A compatible discrete quadratic energy may exist, but constructing and relating it to the advertised energy requires a nontrivial reformulation.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the stated exact-integral potential gives -(hat f(m_h),∂tm_h), not the FV pairing -(hat f(m_h),I_h^*∂tm_h). The exchange term also differentiates to (ε/2)d_t|||m_h|||_h², whereas the displayed identity uses ε times that derivative. Thus the quantity differentiated in the proof is not the energy that was defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the discrete potential and exchange energies using quadratures and quadratic forms exactly compatible with the FV equations, then derive their exact time derivatives and reassess the boundary term.
issues.overall_effect: Even independently of Lemma lem-t, the proof does not establish monotonicity of the stated discrete magnetic free energy.
issues.title: The potential-energy derivative is incompatible with the FV quadrature
issues.why_classification: The energy must be reformulated and its consistency checked; this is more than a local factor correction but need not change the numerical scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: The equations defining g_i use m_i^{n+1}, but the only values available before the final projection are the provisional hat m_i^{n+1}; the projected m^{n+1} is defined only after g_1 and g_2 have already been used. No ordering or identification resolves this circular dependency.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the exact provisional value used as the datum in each g_i solve and give an unambiguous sequential ordering of all solves and component updates.
issues.overall_effect: The time-stepping procedure is not executable as written, so its claimed five heat solves per step and all numerical outputs are not determined by the supplied algorithm.
issues.title: The Gauss-Seidel update depends on not-yet-defined values
issues.why_classification: A local algorithmic redesign or clarification may resolve the circularity, but the source does not determine which update was actually intended.

issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise normalization of a nonconstant piecewise-linear vector field is generally not piecewise linear, so the projected field is not in S_h and cannot be used as the next finite-element iterate. If nodal normalization and interpolation were intended, they are not stated. In addition, no argument or step-size condition ensures that hat m_h is nonzero where the quotient is taken.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define projection at every mesh node followed by finite-element interpolation, and establish nonvanishing of all provisional nodal vectors or prescribe a fallback for zero vectors.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm is not closed in its declared approximation space and is undefined at possible zeros of the provisional field.
issues.title: Pointwise projection does not remain in the finite-element space and may divide by zero
issues.why_classification: The standard nodal projection is a plausible contained repair, but both the finite-element reconstruction and well-definedness condition are mathematically necessary and absent.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof removes Φ from boundary integrals as though it were constant on each segment. The hypothesis only gives a variable Sobolev function Φ, so this equality is invalid. Exact pointwise cancellation of (Φ×∇u)·∇u in the continuous form does not imply exact cancellation in the FV form with the discontinuous test interpolation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Estimate the nonconstant-coefficient remainder, likely as an O(h)||∇Φ|| term, and prove it can be absorbed into the diffusion coercivity for sufficiently small h; then revisit every use of exact cancellation.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted exact zero and the stated proof of coercivity for A_h fail. Consequently the coercivity invoked in the auxiliary error estimates and inherited main theorem is not established.
issues.title: The proof of exact cancellation in the FV cross-product form treats a variable coefficient as constant
issues.why_classification: A small-mesh perturbation argument may preserve coercivity, but it is a new nontrivial estimate and the exact lemma must be weakened.
